IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Monday, September 21, 2026**

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** is the sharp play right now. Thirty hands needed on Port Washington Data Center work through both Gurtz and Cupertino, and both contractors are running **JW wage plus $10/hr base wage increase** — that's real money on top of scale. Wil-Surge and MJ Electric are also holding calls on the same project. Book depth sits solid at ~195 hands across 43 total calls. Data center work means steady hours and locked-in schedules.

**LU-430 Racine, WI** is running hot on Microsoft Mount Pleasant, with all four contractors paying **$62.51/hr**. Gerdes, Pieper, Staff Electric, and Kelso Burnett have 53 combined openings. Book's lean at 76 hands deep, so if you can hit the road immediately, you're in Book 1. Long sleeves and conduit work required — standard DC fit-out discipline.

**LU-237 Niagara Falls, NY** has Ferguson and O'Connell pulling bodies into Lake Mariner Data Center at **$48.20/hr** with per diem incentives and solid 1st shift (6:30 AM–5:00 PM). Seventy-seven hands on the board across just four calls. This is high-ratio work — move fast.

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** sits at 428 hands chasing 59 calls — all rated at **$42/hr** across Miller, Inglett & Stubbs, and Whitehead. QTS Fayetteville and the DC3 halls need cable tray and feeder work. Book depth means you're not locked in, but the work is there.

**LU-575 Portsmouth, OH** just posted Amazon North and South campuses with TSG holding 96 openings starting Sept 28, running **4-10s with occasional Saturdays**. Hanley and Hatzel & Buehler have smaller calls live. ASAP starts mean onboarding this week.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** rounds out the picture: QTS, Meta, and Facebook Eagle Mountain all running 5-day schedules at **$46.22/hr** with overtime plus Saturday availability. 

Data center projects are absorbing hands nationally — the cloud build is still driving dispatch.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Monday, September 21, 2026**

**LU-71 Columbus, OH** is sitting fat with 46 calls and room for ~140 hands. New River Elect Corp is running two separate boards: 40 JLs on 6-10s distro work in Columbus with $125 nightly per diem plus $125 bonus on 10-hour days (CDL required), and 9 more JLs down in Southern Ohio on 4-10s with optional Fri/Sat availability. Capital Electric is splicing cable in Johnstown (6 JLs, OSHA 10 + Class A CDL mandatory). This is volume work with flexible schedules—solid if you're chasing hours over pay.

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is the pay standout on the board. Service Electric's Social Circle jobs hit **$56.80/hr** plus $150/day per diem, and they're offering a **$10/hr premium** over scale for Quanta barehand certification—that's **$66.80/hr** walking in if you hold the cert. Heart Utilities' Savannah run pays **$46.80** on 5-10s. Twenty plus hands needed, TVA/transmission-grade work.

**LU-66 Houston, TX** has 21 calls across three heavy contractors. NHPL is loading 19 JLs onto overhead distro (Class A CDL, all OT double time, $150/day per diem) and 9 more on transmission work in Floresville ($175/day per diem). Front Line is running URD transformer inspections (Class C driver's license sufficient). This is boots-on-the-ground utility work with real per diem dollars.

**LU-1393 Indianapolis, IN** features a $64.66/hr Wanatah rebuild (ARC American, 5 hands) alongside Ampjack's 345kv tower raises at **$56.66/hr** plus $100/day per diem. Kent Power and MJ Electric round out the Valparaiso-to-Fort Wayne corridor on transmission and distribution. Thirty-six calls, solid mid-tier pay, and climbing work if you've got the steel experience.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** is thick with data center and compressor station work. Polaris Forge in Harwood is $44.80/hr on 6-10s with non-taxed $100/day per diem and incentive pay (17 Inside JWs needed). Michels Power bumps to $200/day per diem in St. Vincent on compressor station work. Expect ND/MN licenses required across the board.

**LU-70 Forestville, MD** leads the nation at **$126/hr**—Miller Bros substation work in the DC area with $125/day per diem. Thayer's Shenandoah Valley distro gig pays **$71/hr** plus $125 bonus at 45 hours or $150 at 55. These are specialty substation and high-voltage gigs. Fourteen calls, thirty hands needed.

Data center and transmission work is absorbing hands across every region—the megawatt builds (Polaris, Meta, Google, CVE Llano) are the gravity wells right now.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Monday, September 21, 2026**

**LU-290 Portland, OR** is running hot with 23 calls chasing 47 hands — that's a solid 2:1 ratio favoring workers. The Intel Ronler Acres fab in Hillsboro is the anchor, pulling CAD/BIM detailers, high-purity fitters, orbital welders, and general fitters across multiple tickets through Apollo and Charter Mechanical. These are specialty tool-install roles, not commodity work. Book depth isn't listed, but when you've got that many "Other" classifications firing at one site, you're looking at certified hands moving quick.

**LU-140 Salt Lake City, UT** has the board's fattest single call: the Sego Project in West Valley is pulling 15 journeyman pipefitters and 13 journeyman plumbers through BCS Mechanical on 4-10s starting back in August (so likely ramping or stable through fall). That's 28 hands on one contractor alone. Five apprentices also on that call. DSI's QTS data center in Eagle Mountain is secondary but tighter — 6 journeyman pipefitters on a rotating 5-10s + 1-8 schedule at **$10.00/hr** (that's the specialty rate on that specific call). Eighteen calls total across the local; book's presumably running thin.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** sits at 13 calls for 36 hands. Kiewit's project pull is the headline: **$65.00/hr**, **$65 per diem**, night shift at 15% premium, CWI-certified, 5-10s + Saturday 8s. That's a banger for a night-shift gig. US Eng. Metalworks is running a fab shop with SS fitters and TIG welders in parallel. High-purity tube-bending work at Broadcom in Fort Collins fills the board. Denver's staying tight — this is solid money and moving hands.

**LU-776 Lima, OH** is quietly busy: 4 calls, 25 hands looking. Cenovus (maintenance, fab shop, refinery work) is the backbone across Gem, Graham, and Nooter. Long hours — 6-10s to 7-10s — with spotty OT and incentive pay at **$125/day** noted on the Nooter fab call. Upland's Lima Data Center adds a fourth call at 5-10s + 8s, all OT double time. Refinery and fab work holds bodies.

**LU-525 Las Vegas, NV** is starved: 1 call, 12 hands. Four Seasons towers in Henderson started Thursday 7/30 (journeyman only, OSHA 10/30 required). Call dispatch for details — this board's running on fumes.

Semiconductor and data-center piping is pulling hard across the West; refinery maintenance keeps the Midwest tethered.
